solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: An old cleric accepts extra money from the other side of the world

definitions.text: from the other side of the world

indicators.note: accepts means the cleric phrase takes the money word inside it, like a host letting a guest in

parts.note: taken as written
a dean is a senior cleric in a cathedral
a tip is extra money given for good service

explanation.surface: An elderly clergyman takes a gratuity from someone in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the other side of the world' is a fair definition: Antipodean is the British word for anyone from Australia or New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: Australians and New Zealanders are called Antipodeans by Britons, being from the opposite side of the globe.

clue.text: A little child beginning to yelp, hurting from too much exercise?

parts.note: taken as written
ch. is the dictionary abbreviation for child, so a 'little' child is shortened

indicators.note: beginning to picks out only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A toddler starts to cry, sore after overdoing the exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscles that ache after exertion leave you sore, which is the adjective's sense.

clue.text: Quarrel in that place, mostly on account of one having a flip?

indicators.note: in places the quarrel word inside the shortened place word
mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: there means in that place
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: An argument somewhere, largely about someone tossing something over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the final E of the place word; 'on account of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who flips a coin or pancake tosses it, so is a person doing the throwing.

clue.text: Freedom for Irina Ratushinskaya?

parts.note: Ratushinskaya was a Soviet dissident poet who was jailed, so the clue seems to ask for her release; read instead as the latitude a poet is allowed with grammar and fact

explanation.surface: A call for the release of an imprisoned Russian dissident.
explanation.walkthrough: Irina Ratushinskaya was a Russian poet imprisoned in the Soviet Union in the 1980s; the freedom is the artistic kind given to any writer of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the liberty writers of verse take with rules of language or facts for effect.

clue.text: Feeble salesperson must get with it after end of year

indicators.note: after says the salesperson and the it come behind the year-end piece

parts.note: Dec is short for December, the year's final month
a rep is a sales representative
taken as written

explanation.surface: A weak salesman has to get trendy at the close of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of year' is not the letter R but the last month, DEC.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepit describes someone worn out and weak with age, a synonym of feeble.

clue.text: Girl and boy recorded events of the year

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
Al is a boy's name, short for Alan or Albert

explanation.surface: A girl and a boy wrote down what happened during the year.
explanation.definitionFit: An annal is the chronicle of a single year, a record of its events.

clue.text: Soil given bash, letting in oxygen

indicators.note: letting in means the bash word admits the oxygen symbol inside it

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or bash
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Earth is given a whack, which lets air into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Loam is fertile garden earth of clay, sand and humus, a kind of soil.

clue.text: Fury brought by defeat beginning to end over time

indicators.note: beginning to end means the first letter is shifted to the back of the word

parts.note: a rout is a heavy defeat
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Anger caused by a loss, from start to finish over a period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to end' moves the R of ROUT to the back, making OUTR.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrage is fierce anger at an injustice, a close synonym of fury.

clue.text: Serious thinking? To maiden it may seem strange

indicators.note: strange means the letters are thrown into an odd new order

explanation.surface: Deep contemplation might look odd to a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may seem strange' rearranges TO MAIDEN IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Meditation is deep focused reflection, a form of serious thought.

clue.text: Lots of people in road in Plymouth area

indicators.note: the second in puts the road abbreviation inside the Plymouth place

parts.note: Plymouth Hoe is the famous open seafront area of Plymouth, in Devon

explanation.surface: A crowd on a street somewhere in Plymouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Plymouth Hoe is the seafront park in the English city of Plymouth where Drake reputedly played bowls.
explanation.definitionFit: A horde is a great crowd or throng of people.

clue.text: Strenuous musical performance attended by someone on the paper

parts.note: a concert is a musical performance
an ed, the editor, works on a newspaper

explanation.surface: A demanding recital watched by a newspaper journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A concerted effort is a determined, vigorous one, so strenuous in sense.

clue.text: Be prepared for speech to produce coughing

parts.note: to expect something is to be ready for it
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: Get ready for an address that will make the audience hack.
explanation.definitionFit: Expectoration is the act of bringing up phlegm, done by coughing and spitting.

clue.text: While a pet hen possibly needs time, this creature would be too extravagant a possession!

definitions.text: this creature would be too extravagant a possession

indicators.note: possibly says the words could be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A pet chicken takes time to look after, but this animal would cost far too much to keep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges WHILE A PET HEN, then T is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a costly possession whose upkeep exceeds its use, after the albino beasts of Siamese kings.

clue.text: A man in control of his craft?

definitions.text: A man in control of his craft?

parts.words: A man in control of his craft?
parts.note: seems to praise a skilled artisan's mastery of his trade; craft really means a vessel at sea, so this is its captain

explanation.surface: A skilled craftsman at the top of his trade.
explanation.definitionFit: This title is the captain who commands a merchant ship, a sea craft.

clue.text: Like a design that could have some sinister feature

definitions.text: Like a design that could have some sinister feature

parts.words: Like a design that could have some sinister feature
parts.note: sinister suggests menace, but in coats of arms it is the term for the left-hand side

explanation.surface: A pattern with something ominous lurking in it.
explanation.walkthrough: In heraldry 'sinister' means the left side of a shield as its bearer sees it, as in a bend sinister.
explanation.definitionFit: Coats of arms are designs described in a vocabulary where sinister is a standard side.

clue.text: Stress when money is added to bill

indicators.note: is added to says the money piece comes on the end of the bill piece

parts.note: a/c is short for account, a bill
a cent is a small coin of money

explanation.surface: Anxiety when an extra charge goes on the invoice.
explanation.definitionFit: An accent is the stress placed on a syllable in speech.

clue.text: Bogs with small plants enthralling artist

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the plants hold the artist inside

parts.note: mosses are small flowerless plants
RA, Royal Academician, is the stock crossword artist

explanation.surface: Marshes whose little plants captivate a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A morass is a boggy area of wet ground, a swamp or bog.

clue.text: School — first place for violent revolt

indicators.note: first says the place word comes before the school abbreviation

parts.note: to put is to place

explanation.surface: A school gets top position in an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue names the school before the place, so 'first' is needed to reverse that order in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A putsch is a sudden attempt to overthrow a government, a violent coup.

clue.text: Labour lag behind with introduction of alternative vote?

indicators.note: introduction of means the voting abbreviation is inserted into the lag word

parts.note: to trail is to lag behind
AV is short for the alternative vote, a preferential voting system put to a UK referendum in 2011

explanation.surface: The Labour Party falls behind after bringing in a new voting system.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour looks like the British political party, given the voting talk, but it means toil.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is painful toil or hard work, a synonym of labour.

clue.text: Officer and other ranks having a party somewhere in America

parts.note: Col is short for colonel, an officer
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
taken as written
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Army officers and soldiers celebrating at a party in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Colorado is a US state, so a place in America.

clue.text: Girl of 5, dreadfully idle worm

parts.note: the girl in the answer to 5 down is Ann

indicators.note: dreadfully says the letters are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A young woman of five turns out to be an awfully lazy creature.
explanation.definitionFit: An annelid is a segmented worm, such as an earthworm or leech.

clue.text: A profit on two separate occasions or maybe several times?

parts.note: a gain is a profit
on two separate occasions says the A GAIN piece comes twice, joined by AND
the same piece once more

explanation.surface: Making money twice, or perhaps more often.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'A profit' twice over, linked by AND; 'or maybe' points to the looser sense of repeatedly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means repeatedly, many times over.

clue.text: Certainly not a component of fine verse

indicators.note: component of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Refusing to accept something as part of good poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic refusal, meaning at no time and by no means.

clue.text: Showman with diamonds, modest on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside means the modest word sits around the card suit

parts.note: coy means shy or modest
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: A performer wearing jewels but bashful about it.
explanation.walkthrough: William Cody, Buffalo Bill, ran the Wild West touring show.
explanation.definitionFit: Buffalo Bill Cody was a famous showman of Wild West exhibitions.

clue.text: Robbers? They may get into hot water

definitions.meaning: in Cockney rhyming slang these words stand for thieves, the rhyme on leaves

definitions.text: They may get into hot water
definitions.meaning: the dried bits brewed in a teapot, which literally go into hot water

explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang is a London dialect where a phrase replaces the word it rhymes with; 'get into hot water' looks like being in trouble, apt for robbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Thieves rhyme with leaves in Cockney slang, and the brew's leaves steep in boiling water.

clue.text: One good room in a domed dwelling

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
the loo is a familiar British word for the toilet, a small room

explanation.surface: A single fine room inside a house with a curved roof.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is an Inuit snow house shaped like a dome.

clue.text: Part of member of working class, not leader

indicators.note: not leader means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a prole, from proletarian, is a member of the working class

explanation.surface: Part of a labourer's lot, without a boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not leader' removes the P from PROLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A role is the part played by an actor.

clue.text: Contemporary party needs to be different

indicators.note: to be different means the letters must change into a new order

explanation.surface: A modern celebration needs to stand out from the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of this moment is current, the same as contemporary.
